title: Missed Senate Summons Costs KPC Acting Chief KSh500,000
desc: Senate has fined KPC's acting chief KSh500,000 and renewed summons against senior officials over the unresolved Thange oil spill.
content:
The Senate Energy Committee has fined Kenya Pipeline Company (KPC) Acting Managing Director Pius Mwendwa KSh500,000 after he failed to appear before lawmakers investigating the long-running Thange oil spill in Makueni County.

The decision was made on Thursday, November 19, after the committee ruled that officials who attended the session could not represent the KPC board or answer in place of the company's chief executive.

Mwendwa reportedly explained that he was unable to attend because he had an interview scheduled for the substantive managing director position on the same morning. Committee chairperson and Elgeyo Marakwet Senator William Kisang maintained that parliamentary summons must be honoured personally.

The committee's action has renewed attention on the environmental disaster that began on May 12, 2015, when a petroleum pipeline operated by KPC leaked in Thange, Kibwezi East, releasing oil into the surrounding environment and water sources.

During Thursday's proceedings, Makueni Governor Mutula Kilonzo Jr presented a water sample from the affected river, saying it still carried the smell of petroleum products.

The governor told senators that contamination had extended approximately 42 kilometres along the Thange River. He also disclosed that the Makueni County Government, together with the Ministry of Health, had spent KSh62 million treating affected residents.

These figures were presented during the Senate hearing and should be understood as claims made by the governor to the committee.

The lawmakers also took action over the absence of senior national government officials. Cabinet Secretaries responsible for Health and Energy and Petroleum were summoned after failing to attend the scheduled hearing.

The committee further resolved to bring in the Cabinet Secretaries responsible for Water and Environment, alongside the National Environment Management Authority (NEMA) and the KPC board, to respond to questions surrounding the unresolved pollution.

Makueni Senator Daniel Maanzo also called on the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) to collect the water sample presented during the session for preservation as evidence.

Mwendwa has been directed to appear before the committee again during the first week of December, when the other summoned officials and KPC board representatives are also expected to attend.

The latest Senate intervention places renewed pressure on the responsible institutions to explain what has been done to address the contamination and the concerns raised by communities living along the affected river.
